canonical_source.behavior: The current source enables the destructive Site Settings action only after the user types the exact site name, invokes SiteService.DeleteSiteAsync(Id), and navigates to /sites only after that deletion call succeeds. The caller supplies the current Site Id; identity and tenant ownership are not accepted as editable form data.

laravel_adaptation.behavior: The Site Settings danger-zone form submits a CSRF-protected DELETE to an explicit canonical route. The controller resolves the active tenant from TenantContext, authorizes sites.manage, scopes the site by server-resolved tenant_id plus route site ID, requires an exact case-sensitive server-side site-name confirmation, blocks deletion while a queued/running execution exists, deletes in a transaction under a row lock, rereads authoritatively after commit, clears the deleted active-site session pointer, and redirects to /sites only after absence is proven.

authorization.tenant_resolution: tenant.context plus exact route slug equality with server-resolved TenantContext
authorization.csrf: web middleware plus Blade @csrf and method-spoofed DELETE

tenant_isolation.server_tenant_identity: TenantContext tenant id and slug; submitted tenant_id is ignored
tenant_isolation.server_actor_identity: authenticated request user; submitted actor_user_id is ignored
tenant_isolation.site_resolution: withoutGlobalScopes constrained explicitly by active TenantContext tenant_id and route site primary key
tenant_isolation.caller_selected_identity_fields: not used for authorization, ownership, or target selection

validation.confirmation: required string, maximum 255 characters, then exact case-sensitive equality with the server-loaded site name

secret_safety.request: no credential, API key, provider secret, or WordPress Application Password is required by the delete contract
secret_safety.response: redirect plus fixed status only; submitted fields are not echoed
secret_safety.site_settings_read: existing credential projection remains secret-free and renders only a fixed password mask

truthful_mutation_semantics.active_execution_guard: queued/running executions return 409 before delete and are never implicitly cancelled
truthful_mutation_semantics.session_cleanup: canonical_site_id is removed only when it points at the successfully deleted site
truthful_mutation_semantics.replayed_delete: 404 because the tenant-scoped site no longer exists; no second fake success
truthful_mutation_semantics.retry: no automatic destructive retry; a manual replay must pass the full auth/tenant/site checks and fails closed after a successful prior delete
truthful_mutation_semantics.cancellation: no asynchronous delete job/provider request exists; an unrelated active execution blocks the operation rather than being cancelled

runtime_boundaries.database: tenant-scoped transactional Eloquent delete plus authoritative post-commit existence query
runtime_boundaries.billing_provider: not called despite scanner domain classification

acceptance_tests.coverage: canonical operation route and production marker; web/auth/tenant.context and rendered CSRF token; authenticated sites.manage authorization; server-derived tenant and actor identity; foreign tenant/direct-ID 404; exact-name validation; active-execution fail-closed behavior without implicit cancellation; transactional successful deletion, authoritative absence, active-site session cleanup, ignored spoof identity fields, secret non-echo, and replay 404 semantics

terminality.basis: The destructive Site Settings control is wired to a real tenant-scoped runtime mutation with source-equivalent typed confirmation, deterministic authorization/IDOR/CSRF validation, fail-closed active-operation handling, authoritative persistence verification, and no fabricated success.
